events.title: Section 232 UAS/drone tariffs take effect
events.why_it_matters: 100% duties on larger/thermal UAS and 25% on smaller drones are now live at 12:01 a.m. ET, aimed at China supply chains with 10–15% allied caps.
events.what_to_watch: CBP guidance, allied-origin certifications, and any China retaliation in components or rare-earth inputs.

events.title: ISM Services PMI (August)
events.why_it_matters: Services are most of the US economy; July was 54.1, so another expansion print would sit awkwardly next to a possible Warsh hike and a weak goods-jobs pulse.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 50, prices-paid, and employment sub-indexes as the last activity read before Friday NFP.

events.title: Initial jobless claims (pre-NFP)
events.why_it_matters: Last high-frequency labor print before Friday payrolls; prior week was 203k vs ~208k expected.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~205k; a break above ~220k would strengthen the labor-slowdown case into Warsh's FOMC.

events.title: US August employment report (NFP)
events.why_it_matters: July payrolls fell 23k even as unemployment eased to 4.1%; August is the last jobs print before the Warsh FOMC, with ADP already soft at +38k.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~+55–65k and jobless rate 4.1–4.2%; a second negative print would clash with ~60% hike odds, a hot beat would lock them.

events.title: US August CPI
events.why_it_matters: July was +0.1% m/m / +3.4% y/y (core +0.2% / +2.5%); Warsh called inflation concerning with PCE near 3.7%, and Hormuz oil is feeding the energy channel.
events.what_to_watch: Headline consensus ~+0.3–0.4% m/m, core ~+0.2–0.24%; a hot print all but locks a September hike.

events.title: US August PPI
events.why_it_matters: July final-demand PPI was 0.0% m/m / +4.7% y/y and likely missed late-July oil; August is the pipeline read into CPI and Warsh.
events.what_to_watch: Trading Economics ~+0.3% m/m and a rebound toward ~5% y/y if energy and AI-capex goods pass through.

events.title: FOMC September decision (first Warsh SEP/dots)
events.why_it_matters: Funds rate is 3.50–3.75%; Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech lifted 25bp hike odds into the ~50–70% range, making this the cycle's highest-stakes meeting.
events.what_to_watch: NFP (Sep 4) and CPI (Sep 11) as the gates; dots, SEP inflation path, and whether Warsh frames energy as a one-off or a regime.

events.title: ECB rate decision (Berlin)
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate is 2.25%; euro-area flash CPI jumped to 3.3% y/y in August on energy (+14.3%), and markets price ~80–95% odds of a 25bp hike to 2.50%.
events.what_to_watch: Size of hike, updated staff projections, and whether Lagarde treats Hormuz energy as persistent.

events.title: Bank of Japan policy meeting
events.why_it_matters: Policy rate is 1.0%; Ueda said the board will debate a hike this month as yen weakness and energy import costs lift upside inflation risks.
events.what_to_watch: OIS/prediction markets ~85–96% for +25bp to 1.25%; statement language on the pace of further normalization.

events.title: Bank of England rate decision
events.why_it_matters: Bank Rate is 3.75% after June/July holds; energy volatility has trimmed hike odds versus the ECB's near-certain move.
events.what_to_watch: Vote split versus July's 6-3 against a hike, and whether energy is treated as a UK-specific inflation risk.

events.title: Canada dollar-for-dollar tariffs take effect
events.why_it_matters: Ottawa matches US 50% Section 338 duties on ~$27.6B of US goods (steel, furniture, apparel, dairy, electronics) from 12:01 a.m. Sep 8.
events.what_to_watch: Any last-minute talks, CBSA in-transit exemptions, and US counter-retaliation after Labor Day.

events.title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' iPhone 18 event
events.why_it_matters: First hardware event under CEO John Ternus; expected iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and a rumored first foldable, with base iPhone 18 slipped to spring 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Foldable pricing/volume, ASP mix, and any China/supply commentary after the drone and Canada tariff shocks.

events.title: Adobe Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Software/AI-tools bellwether tests whether generative-AI monetization is offsetting creative-cloud saturation.
events.what_to_watch: Net-new ARR, Firefly/AI attach, and FY guide versus a still-hawkish rate path.

events.title: Oracle Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Cloud-infrastructure print the same day as Adobe is the next test of AI-capex spend beyond Nvidia/Dell/Broadcom hardware.
events.what_to_watch: OCI growth, remaining performance obligations, and any hyperscaler/capacity commentary.

events.title: OPEC+ core-group meeting (October quotas)
events.why_it_matters: Sources expect unchanged October policy after a ~188kbd September quota step; Hormuz disruptions, not quotas, are the binding supply constraint.
events.what_to_watch: Any emergency language on Iran/Hormuz and the end-September capacity review.

events.title: China August trade data
events.why_it_matters: July exports were already +23.9% y/y; August will show whether AI/electronics demand and tariff diversion are still offsetting weak domestic demand.
events.what_to_watch: Export growth vs July's 23.9% and the US/ASEAN mix after Canada and drone-tariff shocks.

events.title: China August CPI/PPI
events.why_it_matters: July CPI was only +0.5% y/y; a still-soft print keeps the easing-bias case alive even as PBoC holds LPR at record lows.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 0.5% and any energy-import pass-through from Hormuz.

events.title: US August retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Drops on FOMC day two and is the consumer-resilience check after Costco's +9.9% August sales and ahead of Canada tariffs.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales versus a possible gasoline-price boost from oil in the $90s.

events.title: US August housing starts
events.why_it_matters: Rate-sensitive housing is the transmission channel if Warsh hikes into already-soft labor.
events.what_to_watch: Starts and permits versus mortgage-rate backup after Jackson Hole.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) day-90 lockup tranche
events.why_it_matters: Staggered post-June IPO unlock (~319M shares around Sep 9, another tranche ~Sep 24) adds float into a hawkish-rate tape.
events.what_to_watch: Actual selling versus unlock size; Musk's longer lock remains into 2027.

events.title: US–Iran strikes reopen Hormuz oil shock
events.why_it_matters: Fresh US airstrikes and Iranian retaliation pushed Brent back into the low-to-mid $90s (WTI high-$80s/low-$90s), reopening the energy-inflation channel for the Fed and ECB.
events.what_to_watch: Tanker transits, further CENTCOM/IRGC strikes, and whether Brent holds above $90 versus a path back toward $100+.

events.title: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 earnings (AI semis test)
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $29.59B and AI semis $16.7B (+221% y/y) confirmed custom-silicon demand after Nvidia/Dell, but Q4 ~$34.8B guide was a touch light and supply bottlenecks were flagged.
events.what_to_watch: After-hours/next-session multiple compression versus AI-networking follow-through into Oracle.

events.title: Snowflake Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Product revenue $1.49B (+37%) and a raise to 36% FY product-growth showed AI/data spend still broadening beyond hardware.
events.what_to_watch: Whether software peers (Adobe/Oracle) corroborate the same AI-attach story.

events.title: HPE Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Record $12.21B revenue (+34%) and a raised FY growth outlook corroborated Dell's AI-server cycle, but shares still sold off after hours.
events.what_to_watch: Networking/AI-server margins versus Dell's $95B backlog as the quality check on the infrastructure supercycle.

events.title: ADP August private payrolls
events.why_it_matters: Private payrolls rose only 38k (vs ~47k) — slowest since January — keeping the labor-slowdown case alive into Friday NFP and Warsh.
events.what_to_watch: Whether BLS NFP confirms the downshift or rebounds toward +55–65k.

events.title: Costco August monthly sales
events.why_it_matters: Net sales $23.70B (+9.9% y/y) and comps +8.4% showed a still-resilient US consumer into a possible Fed hike and Canada tariff shock.
events.what_to_watch: Full Q4 earnings Sep 24 and whether gasoline/FX-ex comps stay above 5%.

events.title: Dell Q2 FY2027 AI-server blowout
events.why_it_matters: Record $47.0B revenue, $16.4B AI-server sales, $60.9B AI orders and a $95B backlog, with FY AI-server guide lifted to $74B.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Broadcom/HPE/Oracle confirm the same demand or flag power/shell/HBM bottlenecks.

events.title: Nvidia Q2 FY2027 ($96.2B) still setting the AI bar
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), data center $89.0B, and Q3 guide $108B ±2% remain the cycle's demand anchor even as China compute is assumed at zero.
events.what_to_watch: Supply constraints, Vera Rubin ramp comments from peers, and any China-export enforcement headlines.

events.title: Trump signs CR through December 11 (October shutdown killed)
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 6500 funds the government through Dec 11 after a 370-48 House vote, removing the October 1 shutdown risk ahead of midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Nothing near-term; the next cliff is Dec 11, after the election.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies: no breakup
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected DOJ's AdX divestiture ask and ordered behavioral remedies, the third major Big Tech structural-breakup miss.
events.what_to_watch: DOJ appeal decision and the still-untried Apple/Amazon cases (2027+).

events.title: Euro-area August flash CPI 3.3%
events.why_it_matters: Headline HICP jumped to 3.3% from 2.9% on energy +14.3%, the highest since Sep 2023, locking high odds of an ECB hike on Sep 10.
events.what_to_watch: Final print mid-September and whether core stays near 2.4%.

events.title: China August PMI: official 49.8 / Caixin 51.5
events.why_it_matters: Official manufacturing stayed in contraction but improved; Caixin expanded for a ninth month on exports, splitting domestic softness vs external AI demand.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 8–9 trade/CPI prints and whether PBoC stays on hold at the Sep 20 LPR.

events.title: Korea August semiconductor exports $46.65B (+209% y/y)
events.why_it_matters: Record chip exports and total exports $98.25B (+68.7%) are the cleanest high-frequency confirmation of the AI hardware boom outside US earnings.
events.what_to_watch: Whether September maintains the $40B+ chip run-rate if oil/rates bite demand.

events.title: SHEIN Hong Kong IPO debut
events.why_it_matters: Priced ~$1.7–1.8B at a ~$26–27B valuation (far below the old $100B private mark) and slipped as much as 10% on debut — a risk-off read on China consumer/IPO windows.
events.what_to_watch: Secondary trading and whether other HK/China consumer listings reprice lower.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI August 54.6
events.why_it_matters: Eighth expansion month but down from 55.6, with prices-paid still 71.1 — activity resilient, inflation pipeline not dead.
events.what_to_watch: Today's services PMI for whether prices-paid stays hot into CPI.

events.title: Warsh Jackson Hole hawkish reset (still gating Sep FOMC)
events.why_it_matters: Chair Warsh's inflation-first speech is why hike odds jumped from the mid-30s into a coin-flip/lean-hike into Sep 15–16.
events.what_to_watch: Whether NFP/CPI let him follow through or force a hold-and-hawk-dots compromise.

events.title: IEEPA national emergency on U.S. bulk-power / foreign grid equipment
events.why_it_matters: Trump invoked IEEPA to restrict acquisition/import/install of foreign-produced bulk-power equipment (transformers, inverters, BESS, relays, industrial controls), with DOE rules due in 120 days, hitting China-linked grid supply just as AI data-center load is stressing the grid.
events.what_to_watch: DOE implementing regs, Covered Foreign Entity list, replacement timelines, and any cost/delay pass-through into utility capex and data-center interconnection.

events.title: OFAC Operation Economic Outcast (Iran sectoral + ~60 designations)
events.why_it_matters: Treasury expanded EO 13902 secondary-sanctions risk to Iran digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping and designated nearly 60 parties/vessels, layering financial isolation onto the Hormuz military shock.
events.what_to_watch: Enforcement against China/HK/UAE facilitators, Hormuz shipping compliance, crypto/gold channels, and the Sep 8 wind-down of suspended general licenses.

events.title: FTC + 22 states sue Amazon over secret ad-auction surcharges
events.why_it_matters: Complaint alleges Amazon converted advertised second-price ad auctions into de facto first-price via hidden surcharges, extracting tens of billions from 1M+ advertisers and likely lifting consumer prices.
events.what_to_watch: W.D. Wash. injunction/monetary claims, Amazon Ads revenue disclosure, and any advertiser bid-shading that hits AMZN high-margin ads.

events.title: Beef TRQ expansion: +300k mt lean trimmings (first tranche open)
events.why_it_matters: Proclamation adds 300,000 mt of lean beef trimmings to the 2026 TRQ in three 100k mt tranches from Sep 1 to ease ground-beef prices, a rancher-opposed supply shock into grocery inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 1–30 tranche fill, ground-beef retail prices into CPI, and whether Trump terminates the quota if the 25% import-discount condition is missed.

events.title: JOLTS July job openings 7.271M
events.why_it_matters: Openings were little changed at 7.271M (4.4%) after a downward June revision, a still-cool labor-demand print into Friday NFP and the Warsh FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Quits vs layoffs mix and whether Friday payrolls confirm the openings plateau rather than a layoff break.

events.title: UMich August final: sentiment 51.7, year-ahead inflation 4.0%
events.why_it_matters: Sentiment fell to 51.7 from 55.2 while 1-year inflation expectations eased only to 4.0% (long-run stuck at 3.3%), a hawkish-expectations mix for Warsh even as the consumer mood deteriorated.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 11 preliminary UMich (same morning as CPI) for whether Hormuz oil re-accelerates short-run inflation expectations.

events.title: EIA crude inventories −4.5 mb (week ended Aug 28)
events.why_it_matters: Commercial crude drew 4.5 mb to 424.5 mb, far more than the ~0.3–1.1 mb expected, with refinery utilization near 98% — a tight physical overlay on the Hormuz premium.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 10 EIA (Labor Day delay) and whether SPR (−3.1 mb in the same week) keeps drawing into $90s Brent.

events.title: CrowdStrike Q2 FY2027 beat-and-raise
events.why_it_matters: Cyber bellwether printed $1.47B revenue (+26%), $5.84B ARR, record $333M net-new ARR and raised FY net-new ARR growth — AI-security spend still broadening beyond mega-cap hardware.
events.what_to_watch: Q3 $1.523–1.529B guide conversion and whether Falcon Flex/$2.29B ARR stays the growth engine vs multiple compression into FOMC.

events.title: Salesforce Q2 FY2027: Agentforce + raised FY guide
events.why_it_matters: Cloud-software bellwether did $11.35B revenue, $33.5B cRPO (+14% cc), Agentforce ARR $1.5B and lifted FY revenue to $46.1–46.4B — a software-AI offset to the hardware-heavy primary tape.
events.what_to_watch: Q3 $11.42–11.50B guide, Informatica contribution quality, and whether investment gains (Anthropic) are stripped by the Street.

events.title: Deere Q3 FY2026: construction/turf offset, FY NI raised
events.why_it_matters: Ag-equipment bellwether beat with $12.61B sales and $5.10 EPS as Construction & Forestry OP jumped 84% while Production & Precision Ag sales fell 6%; management called 2026 the cycle bottom and raised FY NI to $4.75–5.00B.
events.what_to_watch: Early-order programs, used-inventory, Brazil/Europe weakness, and whether a Warsh hike delays the claimed ag trough.

events.title: Treasury 10-year and 30-year reopenings
events.why_it_matters: Refunding reopenings (~$39B 10s Sep 9, ~$22B 30s Sep 10, settle Sep 15) hit into CPI/PPI week and the first Warsh FOMC, so tail demand is a live rates-volatility event.
events.what_to_watch: Bid-to-cover, dealer vs international take-down, and 10s/30s stop-through vs the Sep 3 announcement sizes.

events.title: US August existing-home sales
events.why_it_matters: July sales were already 4.06M (−1.7% m/m); August is the housing-demand read into a possible Warsh hike and sits the same day as PPI.
events.what_to_watch: SAAR vs 4.06M, months' supply vs 4.6, and median price vs $434.1k as mortgage-rate sensitivity into FOMC.

events.title: UK August CPI (pre-BoE)
events.why_it_matters: ONS prints August CPI the day before the Sep 17 BoE decision; July was already 2.9% y/y and energy from Hormuz is the upside risk versus a still-less-hawkish MPC than the ECB.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 2.9%, energy/core split, and whether hike odds reprice from the current hold-biased setup.

top_risks: Hormuz/Iran re-escalation pushing Brent back toward $100+ and importing energy inflation into US CPI and ECB/Fed reaction functions
Hot August CPI (Sep 11) locking a Warsh 25bp hike on Sep 15–16 with hawkish dots
NFP surprise on Sep 4: a second negative print is a growth scare, a hot beat is a hike lock — both move BROAD
Canada dollar-for-dollar tariffs on Sep 8 hitting US goods, retailers, and already-sticky goods inflation
Synchronized tightening: ECB (~80–95% hike Sep 10) plus BOJ (~85–96% hike Sep 17–18) plus a possible Fed hike
top_opportunities: AI infrastructure confirmation still running (Nvidia $96.2B, Dell $95B backlog, Broadcom AI $16.7B, Korea chips +209%) into Oracle on Sep 10
Soft NFP + cool core CPI path that forces a Warsh hold and a duration/quality rally
Hormuz de-escalation that unwinds the oil/inflation premium and hike odds in one session
Apple foldable/iPhone 18 Pro event (Sep 9) as a consumer-hardware offset if pricing/volume land
October US shutdown risk now dead (CR signed through Dec 11), removing a midterms-season left tail
summary: September 3 is a pre-NFP data day (claims, ISM Services) with Section 232 drone tariffs already live, while Brent sits in the low-to-mid $90s after this week's US–Iran flare rather than the earlier-war $120 spike. The policy path is still binary: Warsh hike odds ~50–70% into Sep 15–16, gated by Friday's NFP (~+55–65k after July's -23k and ADP +38k) and Sep 11 CPI, with the ECB now an ~80–95% hike on Sep 10 after euro-area inflation hit 3.3%. Offsets are Dell/Nvidia/Broadcom/Korea chip confirmation, a signed CR that kills the October shutdown, and Oracle/Apple next week; Canada's tariffs still hit Sep 8.

catcher.coverage_assessment: Primary was strong on mega-cap AI earnings, the Warsh/ECB/BoJ rate path, NFP/CPI, Canada tariffs, the CR, and the Hormuz military shock, but almost entirely skipped executive/agency actions and second-tier labor, housing, auctions, and software/ag earnings. The government blind spot is the real miss: IEEPA grid emergency, OFAC's Iran campaign, FTC-Amazon, and the beef TRQ never appeared.
catcher.biggest_gap: August 26 IEEPA national emergency restricting foreign bulk-power equipment — a live China/grid/AI-power supply-chain rule with DOE regs due in 120 days that the primary never mentioned.
